You are the verifier for a code review of PR #1714 in /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ (branch already checked out locally: fix/issue-1713-incident-evidence-airflow-run-id-colon). The diff changes `_upstream_pipeline_layer` in backend/app/services/incident_evidence.py to fix issue #1713.

Read backend/app/services/incident_evidence.py (full file, especially lines 167-216), backend/app/db/models.py (PipelineRun model ~line 692-717, and ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS ~line 79), and backend/app/services/orchestration_service.py (marker construction ~line 246-260, and dbt job_name / pipeline_or_dag_id source if relevant — check backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py around lines 244,268 for how pipeline_or_dag_id is populated for dbt).

For each candidate below, return exactly one verdict: CONFIRMED, PLAUSIBLE, or REFUTED, with a one-sentence reason. Use the recall-biased policy: PLAUSIBLE by default unless you can prove impossibility or factual wrongness by quoting code.

CANDIDATE 1 (correctness, high severity): The new lookup in `_upstream_pipeline_layer` filters `PipelineRun.provider == provider` AND `func.concat(PipelineRun.provider, ":", PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id, ":", PipelineRun.provider_run_id) == marker`, then takes `.first()` with no ORDER BY. Because the marker format has no escaping, two different valid PipelineRun rows (different provider_run_id — allowed since only (provider, provider_run_id) is DB-unique, not pipeline_or_dag_id) can produce an IDENTICAL concatenated string if a colon "shifts" between pipeline_or_dag_id and provider_run_id — e.g. Row A: pipeline_or_dag_id="nightly:etl", provider_run_id="abc" vs Row B: pipeline_or_dag_id="nightly", provider_run_id="etl:abc" — both concat to "dbt:nightly:etl:abc". Verify: (a) is pipeline_or_dag_id actually unconstrained/free-form for at least one provider (check dbt's job_name ingestion), so a colon could realistically appear in it; (b) does nothing else in the schema/code prevent this collision; (c) would `.first()` genuinely return a nondeterministic/wrong row in this scenario.

CANDIDATE 2 (correctness, low severity): The old `_parse_orchestration_marker` explicitly rejected a marker whose parsed pipeline or provider_run_id part was empty (`if not sep2 or not pipeline or not provider_run_id: return None`). The new code has no equivalent explicit empty-string rejection — it relies on the DB match failing naturally. Verify whether this is a real (if narrow) regression: could a PipelineRun row with an empty-string `pipeline_or_dag_id` or `provider_run_id` exist (check for NOT NULL vs CHECK constraints enforcing non-empty on those two columns in models.py), such that the new code's behavior differs from the old code's for some malformed marker.

CANDIDATE 3 (cleanup/reuse, low severity): Line ~175 in incident_evidence.py hardcodes the literal tuple `("adf", "airflow", "dbt")` for the provider-prefix check, instead of importing `ORCHESTRATION_PROVIDERS` from backend/app/db/models.py (which is already imported/reused by many other modules per a grep). Verify this constant exists, is exported, and that incident_evidence.py does NOT currently import it (check the import block at the top of the file). Note: this hardcoded tuple was NOT newly introduced by this PR — it existed identically in the deleted `_parse_orchestration_marker` function — but it IS present in the diff's added lines (moved inline). Note this fact in your verdict reasoning.

CANDIDATE 4 (efficiency/simplification, low-medium severity): The new `func.concat(...) == marker` filter can't use the existing `UniqueConstraint("provider", "provider_run_id", name="uq_pipeline_runs_provider_run")` index — it forces Postgres to compute a per-row string concatenation across all PipelineRun rows matching `provider` (bounded by the composite index `ix_pipeline_runs_provider_pipeline(provider, pipeline_or_dag_id)`'s leading column, not a full table scan, but not an exact-match seek either). Verify: is this query on a hot path or a rare path (check where `_upstream_pipeline_layer`/`build_evidence` is called from — search for callers), and is the performance concern realistic given PipelineRun accumulates rows indefinitely (check for any retention/purge sweep on the `pipeline_runs` table).

Return your verdicts as a compact list: candidate number → verdict → one-sentence reason.

You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. - dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). 30	def _layer(name: str, fn: Callable[[], Any]) -> Any:
31	    """Run one evidence layer best-effort: any failure logs a structured warning
32	    and degrades that layer to ``None`` — never poisoning the card (and through
33	    it the whole run's incident sync).
34	    """
35	    try:
36	        return fn()
37	    except Exception:
38	        log.warning("incident_evidence_layer_failed", layer=name)
39	        return None

42	def _num(value: Decimal | None) -> float | None:
43	    """Widen a NUMERIC metric to a JSON-friendly float (``None`` stays ``None``)."""
44	    return float(value) if value is not None else None
45

47	def _iso(value: datetime | None) -> str | None:
48	    return value.isoformat() if value is not None else None

51	def build_evidence(
52	    session: Session,
53	    *,
54	    run: Run,
55	    result: Result,
56	    check: Check | None,
57	    asset: Asset | None,
58	) -> dict[str, Any]:
59	    """Assemble the layer-1 evidence card for a breaching ``result`` on ``run``."""
60	    return {
61	        "generated_at": _utc_now_iso(),
62	        "check": _layer("check", lambda: _check_layer(check)),
63	        "asset": _layer("asset", lambda: _asset_layer(asset)),
64	        "failing_result": _layer("failing_result", lambda: _failing_result_layer(result)),
65	        "metric_trend": _layer(
66	            "metric_trend", lambda: _metric_trend_layer(session, check_id=result.check_id)
67	        ),
68	        "sibling_checks": _layer(
69	            "sibling_checks",
70	            lambda: _sibling_checks_layer(session, run=run, exclude_check_id=result.check_id),
71	        ),
72	        "upstream_pipeline_run": _layer(
73	            "upstream_pipeline_run", lambda: _upstream_pipeline_layer(session, run=run)
74	        ),
75	        "downstream_blast_radius": _layer(

83	
84	def _utc_now_iso() -> str:

87	
88	def _check_layer(check: Check | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
89	    if check is None:

91	    return {

98	
99	def _asset_layer(asset: Asset | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:

104	        "namespace": asset.namespace,
105	        "name": asset.name,
106	        "env": asset.env,
107	    }

109	
110	def _failing_result_layer(result: Result) -> dict[str, Any]:
111	    """The breaching result — status + metric + GX aggregates. **No sample rows.**
112	    ``sample_failures`` is never read.
113	    """
114	    return {
115	        "status": result.status,
116	        "metric_value": _num(result.metric_value),
117	        "observed_value": _strip_sample_lists(result.observed_value),
118	        "expected_value": result.expected_value,
119	    }

122	def _strip_sample_lists(observed: dict[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
123	    """Drop the list-valued sample-bearing keys from an ``observed_value`` dict
124	    (see ``_SAMPLE_LIST_KEYS``); non-dict / ``None`` shapes pass through.
125	    """
126	    if not isinstance(observed, dict):
127	        return observed
128	    return {key: val for key, val in observed.items() if key not in _SAMPLE_LIST_KEYS}
129

131	def _metric_trend_layer(session: Session, *, check_id: uuid.UUID) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
132	    """The last ``_TREND_LIMIT`` readings for the check (newest first) — the
133	    ``metric_value`` trend that distinguishes a sudden break from a slow drift.
134	    """
135	    rows = session.execute(
136	        select(Result.status, Result.metric_value, Result.created_at, Result.run_id)
137	        .where(Result.check_id == check_id)
138	        .order_by(Result.created_at.desc())
139	        .limit(_TREND_LIMIT)
140	    ).all()
141	    return [

143	            "status": status,
144	            "metric_value": _num(metric_value),
145	            "created_at": _iso(created_at),
146	            "run_id": str(run_id),
147	        }
148	        for status, metric_value, created_at, run_id in rows
149	    ]

152	def _sibling_checks_layer(
153	    session: Session, *, run: Run, exclude_check_id: uuid.UUID
154	) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
155	    """The other checks' outcomes in the same run (context: is the asset broadly
156	    unhealthy or is this one check the outlier?). Names via a single join.
157	    """
158	    rows = session.execute(
159	        select(Check.name, Result.status)
160	        .join(Check, Check.id == Result.check_id)
161	        .where(Result.run_id == run.id, Result.check_id != exclude_check_id)
162	        .order_by(Check.name)
163	    ).all()
164	    return [{"check_name": name, "status": status} for name, status in rows]

167	def _upstream_pipeline_layer(session: Session, *, run: Run) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
168	    """The orchestration pipeline run that triggered this suite run, + its delay

170	    """
171	    marker = run.triggered_by

174	    provider, sep, _rest = marker.partition(":")
175	    if not sep or provider not in ("adf", "airflow", "dbt"):
176	        return None

178	    # Airflow DAG run's default `run_id`, "manual__2026-08-08T01:30:00+00:00")
179	    # can itself contain colons, so there is no reliable place to cut the
180	    # "<provider>:<pipeline_or_dag_id>:<provider_run_id>" marker to recover it

188	            PipelineRun.provider == provider,

190	                PipelineRun.provider,
191	                ":",
192	                PipelineRun.pipeline_or_dag_id,
193	                ":",
194	                PipelineRun.provider_run_id,

196	            == marker,

199	    if pipeline_run is None:

201	    return {
202	        "provider": pipeline_run.provider,
203	        "pipeline_or_dag_id": pipeline_run.pipeline_or_dag_id,
204	        "provider_run_id": pipeline_run.provider_run_id,
205	        "status": pipeline_run.status,
206	        "started_at": _iso(pipeline_run.started_at),
207	        "finished_at": _iso(pipeline_run.finished_at),

content.text:
Confirmed the constant is widely reused across the codebase, supporting the reuse claim. Now finalizing verdicts.

**Verdicts:**

**Candidate 1 → CONFIRMED.** `pipeline_or_dag_id` (dbt's `job_name`, `backend/app/orchestration/dbt.py:244/268`) and `provider_run_id` (`invocation_id`) are free-form strings from an external payload with only a `String(256)` column and no format/CHECK constraint disallowing `:` (models.py's `PipelineRun.__table_args__` only checks `provider`/`status`), and the DB-unique constraint is `(provider, provider_run_id)` only — `pipeline_or_dag_id` isn't part of it. So two distinct rows, e.g. `pipeline_or_dag_id="nightly:etl", provider_run_id="abc"` vs `pipeline_or_dag_id="nightly", provider_run_id="etl:abc"`, both legally insertable (different `provider_run_id`), concatenate to the identical string `"dbt:nightly:etl:abc"`. `.first()` with no `ORDER BY` on an ambiguous match is genuinely nondeterministic/could return the wrong pipeline run's evidence. The new code's own comment ("correct regardless of how many colons either part contains") is factually wrong — concatenation without escaping the delimiter is not an injective encoding.

**Candidate 2 → REFUTED.** Traced every writer of `Run.triggered_by`: the only one using an `adf:`/`airflow:`/`dbt:`-prefixed marker is `orchestration_service._trigger_suites` (`marker = f"{provider}:{update.pipeline_or_dag_id}:{update.provider_run_id}"`, line 250), and every provider's `parse_event`/poll path (`dbt.py:247-256`, and the equivalent `if not value`/`if status is None or not dag_id or not run_id` guards in `airflow.py`/`adf.py`) rejects an empty `job_name`/`dag_id`/`pipeline` or `invocation_id`/`run_id` before a `RunUpdate` is ever built. All other `triggered_by` producers use `manual:`/`probe:`/`schedule:`/`mcp:` prefixes that fail the `provider not in (...)` guard immediately.
